identity.name: Revolt of Inaros II
alt_names: Egyptian revolt against Achaemenid Persia (460-454 BC)

land.text: the Nile Delta around Sais and the Libyan coast from Mareia
the Delta around Sais, retaken by Megabyzus in 454

capitals.name: Sais (Sa el-Hagar)
capitals.note: The page names no capital; the Delta "around Sais" is the land he held, so Sais is the researcher's reading.

rulers.name: Inaros II
rulers.note: Infobox: reign c. 460, died c. 454 BC at Susa.

correction.text: a kingship over the Libyans from Mareia (above Pharos) and the part of the Nile Delta around Sais

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; the page gives no area or frontier. Amyrtaeus, also from Sais, held the northern marshes. The Persians kept the Memphis citadel (White Castle). Radii of 80 km at Sais and 60 km at Alexandria (for Mareia, which the gazetteer lacks) are the researcher's reading.

region.text: Mareia and the Delta around Sais

ledger.note: 460: Inaros II raises Libyans and the western Delta against Persia. "In 460 BC, he revolted against the Persians." He "held a kingship over the Libyans from Mareia (above Pharos) and the part of the Nile Delta around Sais."
460: the rebels meet the Persian army and besiege the Memphis citadel. Achaemenes was "defeated and killed at Papremis"; the White Castle at Memphis "could not be dislodged".
454: the revolt is crushed: Megabyzus "finally defeated" Inaros and his Athenian allies (27th Dynasty page).

region.text: Mareia and the Delta around Sais

ledger.note: 454: the Delta returns to Persia. The Inaros II page: "the Athenians were finally defeated in 454 BC by the Persian army"; Inaros was taken to Susa and executed. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Region widened to the found region (Sais and Alexandria radius for Mareia) so that the whole rebel land returns to the Twenty-seventh Dynasty.
454: the rebel kingdom of Inaros II ends; he died c. 454 at Susa.

wars.name: Revolt of Inaros II

zones.text: the Delta around Sais and Mareia

wars.outcome: The revolt failed; the Athenian fleet and army were lost on Prosopitis after an eighteen-month siege.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; the land is "the part of the Nile Delta around Sais" and the Libyan coast.

sources.title: Twenty-seventh Dynasty of Egypt
sources.note: The revolt in the Persian dynasty's account.

notes: Rebel state (rule 5): six years, land held. The Inaros II page names the Delta around Sais and Mareia; the 27th Dynasty page says he took Memphis and was 'substantially assisted by the Athenians of Greece', the Inaros II page that Persian troops held the Memphis citadel. Mareia is not in the gazetteer; an Alexandria radius stands in (name needed: Mareia / Marea, on Lake Mareotis west of Alexandria). The page's date of Inaros's death (c. 454) agrees with Thucydides as read by Bigwood; no other page was opened.
